items.title: Why TLP should not replace your internal information classification, (Sat, Oct 10th)
items.content: <article>The Traffic Light Protocol (TLP)[1], which is now in its second incarnation, is a wonderful standard that enables one to easily communicate whether information may be shared further (and if so, how far).</article>

items.title: ISC Stormcast For Friday, October 9th, 2026 https://isc.sans.edu/podcastdetail/10130, (Fri, Oct 9th)
Reconstructing AI Agent Activity: Two New Scripts for Forensic Review, (Thu, Oct 8th)
items.content: <article>We just did a major update to FOR577 and added a lot of new material on day 5 about investigating AI usage in incident response. In the new material we dicsuss 8 of the most popular AI coding assistants and agents including Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, Copilot, Warp, Windsurf, and Qwen Code. I've been using Claude Code and a little bit of Codex, but I also have recently been playing with OpenCode and am setting up Hermes. I decided to figure out where the chat history was in OpenCode and where any Hermes evidence might be located.</article>

items.title: ISC Stormcast For Thursday, October 8th, 2026 https://isc.sans.edu/podcastdetail/10128, (Thu, Oct 8th)
Scans for Atlassian vulnerablity (CVE-2026-21589), (Wed, Oct 7th)
items.content: <article>On October 5th, Atlassian published patches for multiple products to fix an "Arbitrary File Access" vulnerability [CVE-2026-21589]. An attacker can read arbitrary files in the web application's directory, potentially exposing sensitive information such as configuration files.</article>

More RMM Tools In the Wild, (Tue, Oct 6th)
items.content: <article>It seems that a trend started… I continue my journey discovering more RMM ("Remote Management & Monitoring") tools abused by threat actors! A few days ago, I wrote a diary[1] about ScreenConnect used in the wild. Today, I found another one.</article>

TTY Logs and the Data it Captures, (Sun, Oct 4th)
items.content: <article>For an experiment, I created a script [1] that parses and send the TTY logs collected from actors or bots activity that run various commands after they successfully login the DShield sensor. Those TTY logs are sent daily at the end of each day to the DShield SIEM [2] to be correlated with all the data. </article>
